prompt: A chat app must show new messages to the recipient within 100 ms, without the client polling.
why: Keep a persistent connection so the server pushes messages instantly.
trap: A queue moves messages between services, but the last hop to the phone needs a push channel.

prompt: A sports app shows live scores that change every few seconds to a million connected fans.
why: Push updates over open connections (WebSockets or server-sent events).
trap: Polling a CDN every second multiplies requests and still lags.

prompt: In a shared whiteboard, everyone should see others' cursors move in real time.
tells: see others' cursors move in real time
why: A bidirectional connection streams small updates both ways with minimal latency.
trap: Event logs help with history, but live cursors need low-latency push.

prompt: Riders watch their driver's car move on the map until pickup, updating every second.
why: Push location updates down an open connection.
trap: A geo index finds nearby drivers; tracking one known driver is a push problem.

prompt: A trading screen must show price changes the instant they happen, many times per second.
why: A persistent connection lets the server push each update.
trap: Polling every second is too slow and too wasteful.

prompt: Show "Alex is typing…" to the other person in a chat as it happens.
why: Push small ephemeral events over an open connection.
trap: Too short-lived to store and fetch.

prompt: Mobile clients poll for new notifications every 5 seconds, and 99% of polls return nothing, wasting server capacity and battery.
tells: poll for new notifications every 5 seconds
why: Push (WebSockets or native push) delivers only when there's news.
trap: Caching makes empty polls cheaper, but they're still empty.

prompt: Two million clients hold open WebSocket connections across 40 servers, and a message for one user must reach whichever server holds their connection.
tells: hold open WebSocket connections across 40 servers
why: Track user→server mapping (or use pub/sub) so any server can route the message to the right connection.
trap: The balancer spreads connections; delivery needs a connection registry.
